title: How Labor Strikes Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how labor strikes work: the history of strikes from the late 1700s (early printers' strike in Philadelphia), union bargaining power against employer monopsony, strike types (sick-out/blue flu, slowdown, sit-down, sympathy, general, wildcat), picketing and the word "scab," informational picketing and the Fight for Fifteen, sports strikes (1987 NFL replacement players, 1994 MLB strike and canceled World Series, 2004 NHL lockout, 2012 NFL referee lockout), strikebreaking tactics (Pinkerton agency, Homestead strike of 1892, Great Railroad Strike of 1877), the Wagner Act, Taft-Hartley, permanent replacement, lockouts (American Crystal Sugar lockout in Minnesota), and the 1981 PATCO air traffic controller strike under Reagan. Opens with tour announcements and closes with a listener mail segment about ship name prefixes.

segments.title: Tour announcements and opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts announce tour dates, including Brooklyn shows at the Bell House and ticket sales via the website, then joke about not being on strike.

segments.title: Strike definition and early history
segments.summary: The word strike's origins, early strikes such as Philadelphia printers, and how unions gave workers bargaining power against a single employer (monopsony).

segments.title: Unions, strikes as last resort, and strike duration
segments.summary: Strikes as a last resort after bargaining, the need for a member vote, war chests, average strike length in the US, and comparisons with Europe.

segments.title: Wildcat strikes and Blackfoot tangent
segments.summary: Wildcat strikes happen without union approval. The hosts digress into the Southern rock band Blackfoot.

segments.title: Grievances, contract negotiations and types of strikes
segments.summary: Grievances and bargaining come first; strikes usually happen during contract negotiations. Sick-outs and blue flu, slowdowns, and sit-down strikes are described.

segments.title: Sympathy strikes and general strikes
segments.summary: Sympathy strikes by other unions, the 1981 PATCO strike's lack of support, and general strikes such as those in France.

segments.title: Picketing, scabs, and informational pickets
segments.summary: Picketing draws public support, union membership matters, the origin of the term scab, informational picketing, and the Fight for Fifteen campaign against McDonald's.

segments.title: Sports strikes and lockouts in pro leagues
segments.summary: NFL 1987 strike and replacement players, MLB 1994 strike and canceled World Series, NHL 2004 lockout, and 2012 NFL referee lockout.

segments.title: Strikebreaking, Pinkertons, and Wagner and Taft-Hartley acts
segments.summary: Employers hired Pinkerton detectives; the Homestead battle; the 1877 strike; Wagner Act right to strike; Supreme Court allowing permanent replacement; Taft-Hartley limits on secondary boycotts and closed shops; right-to-work laws.

segments.title: Lockouts and the American Crystal Sugar lockout
segments.summary: Lockouts explained, Supreme Court rulings on temporary replacement, and the 2011 Minnesota American Crystal Sugar lockout.

segments.title: PATCO air traffic controller strike and closing remarks
segments.summary: The 1981 air traffic controller strike under Reagan, firings, replacements, and outcome; hosts suggest further episodes on Flint sit-down strike and Homestead.

segments.title: Listener mail: ship name prefixes
segments.summary: A Navy lieutenant writes about ship name prefixes like USS, HMS, and SS.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts ask for listener contact and sign off.
